title: Dependency Security Remediation

security_findings.vulnerability: JS-YAML DoS / exponential parsing / quadratic CPU consumption advisories

vulnerability_identified.summary: js-yaml: Exponential parsing time in flow collections leads to denial of service

secondary_conflict.summary: JS-YAML: Quadratic CPU consumption in !!omap resolution (3.x and 4.x) — CVE-2026-59870 fix not backported

remediation_performed: Reviewed root and backend package manifests.
Inspected npm lock state and audited dependency tree.
Attempted the minimal non-breaking patch by pinning @nestjs/swagger to 11.4.5.
Confirmed that this only changes js-yaml from 5.2.1 to 4.3.0 and triggers a different high-severity advisory.
Reverted the attempted remedial change to avoid forcing an unsafe dependency upgrade while documenting the blocker clearly.

npm_audit_result.note: The package ecosystem currently provides no safe, consistent fixed version for this dependency chain. The latest version still points to a vulnerable js-yaml, and the previous patch still points to another vulnerable js-yaml minor line.

npm_ls_result.conclusion: No valid safe dependency resolution exists in the currently supported @nestjs/swagger range without a broader ecosystem change or major package update that is outside the scope of this minimal remediation task.

risk_summary: The current @nestjs/swagger package family does not provide a simultaneously safe js-yaml version. A patch attempt reversed to 11.4.5 still leaves a different high-severity js-yaml issue. This is an upstream library incompatibility rather than a code-level issue in the application.
